claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with characteristic phase distributions and internal boundaries.
The proposed framework explicitly incorporates spatial phase distributions, twin boundaries, and grain substructures.
The framework will predict Young's modulus more accurately than conventional physics-based simulations.
The framework will predict yield strength more accurately than conventional physics-based simulations.
The framework will predict fracture behavior more accurately than conventional physics-based simulations.
The framework will produce predictions more rapidly than conventional physics-based simulations.
Nano- to microscale phase distributions, twin boundaries, and grain-boundary networks mediate local deformation and damage accumulation.
The hierarchical heterostructure influences local stress distributions.
The hierarchical heterostructure influences crack nucleation.
Measured training data allow the model to learn nonlinear relationships between heterostructural features and macroscopic mechanical properties.
The framework will reduce prediction error by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional simulations.
The framework will deliver predictions roughly one order of magnitude faster than conventional simulations.
The model may fail at extreme strain rates or high temperatures because those regimes are insufficiently represented by the captured descriptors or training data.
The model may fail when specimen microstructural heterogeneity deviates significantly from the training dataset.
The estimated accuracy gains are based on preliminary trends from multiscale data integration.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% statistically significant improvement in prediction error would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to reduce prediction time by nearly one order of magnitude would falsify the hypothesis.
